parts.layout_phase: Sub-period IA (Period I in the 1970-71 report); the stone rampart, bastions and gateway complex exposed today are the Sub-period IC rebuilding on the same line
parts.what_was_built: The first settlers built the citadel: 'The excavations show that the earliest occupants of Surkotada were Harappans having some affiliation with antecedent culture. These Harappans built a 'citadel' with mud-brick and mud-lump fortification having a rubble veneer of five to eight courses at its base on its inner side over a raised ground of hard yellow rammed earth (average height 1.50 m). The basal width of the rampart was approximately 7 m.' A mud-brick buttress was added on the eastern side later in IA, and the citadel had entrances on the south and the east (Joshi 1990, p. 21). The season reports say the settlement 'was found to be fortified from the very beginning and consisted of a citadel and a lower city adjoining each other' (IAR 1970-71, p. 13) and note four constructional stages in the IA rampart (IAR 1971-72, p. 16). The enclosure kept its area through the whole occupation: 'The area of citadel and residential complexes remained the same through the successive subperiods' (Joshi 1990, p. 17); in IB the IA rampart was reused with a revetment (p. 47). In IC 'the fortifications of the citadel and the lower residential annexe were reconstructed in stone', with corner bastions and a southern gateway complex (IAR 1971-72, p. 17); the IC western rampart 'is built over the earlier mud brick rampart of Period IA' (Joshi 1990, p. 49). The citadel interior measures 60 by 60 m in IC (p. 49).
parts.excavator_basis: Radiocarbon. Joshi writes that 'the Sub-period IA of Surkotada is to be dated between 2055 B.C. to 1970 B.C. or if we take the earliest date of Period IB, 1940 B.C.', from TF-1305 (earliest IA) and TF-1310 (latest IA), quoting B.C. dates computed on the 5730-year half-life with 1950 as reference year and uncalibrated (Joshi 1974, p. 36). The 1990 memoir repeats this and adds PRL-85: IA 'is to be dated between 2055 B.C. (if not 2315 B.C.) to 1970 B.C. or 1940 B.C. (TF 1295)' (Joshi 1990, p. 62). Joshi adds cross-dating that points earlier: Reserved Slip Ware in IA matches Sargonid levels at Brak and other West Asian sites, 'dated to 2371-2316 B.C.' (1974, pp. 35-36; 2370-2284 B.C. in 1990, p. 61), and he concludes that 'the movement of Harappans to Kutch took place at an early stage by circa 2300 B.C. when Surkotada was established' (1974, p. 36; 1990, p. 63). He also notes that only 85 years for the 4.40 m IA deposit in the citadel 'is too short a span' (1990, p. 62).

radiocarbon.phase: not stated; the list describes the site as 'a fortified Harappan site' and the sample as 'Harappa culture'
radiocarbon.note: The list prints '1890 BC'. Joshi 1974 and Joshi 1990 do not mention this date. Joshi lists trench B1 among the citadel's Period IA house remains, with a phase ii wall built on Layer 20 and sealed by Layer 18 (Joshi 1990, p. 44); Layer 17 is therefore above that wall, but Joshi assigns no phase to it.

radiocarbon.phase: Surkotada Period I ('can only be attributed to Surkotada Period I')
radiocarbon.curve: not stated; averages in the table from the Stuiver program of 1986 (Stuiver and Pearson 1986)
radiocarbon.note: Printed as 'TF-1301, 2005 ±130 B.C. (2550-2125 B.C.)'. 2005 B.C. corresponds to the list's 3840 BP on the 5730-year half-life (3840 x 1.03 minus 1950), but Possehl does not state the convention for this line, so we leave the BP fields empty.

syntheses.statement: Possehl and Raval calibrate the Surkotada dates and give an average of 2295 B.C. for Surkotada IA, concluding that 'Radiocarbon determinations from Lothal and Surkotada (Table 1) can be used to suggest that the Urban Phase Sindhi Harappans settled in Gujarat, including Kutch, ca. 2500-2300 B.C.'
syntheses.disagreement: Calibration moves the start of IA, and with it the building of the fortified citadel and annexe, about 250 to 450 years earlier than Joshi's radiocarbon range of 2055-1970 B.C., which is uncalibrated; it agrees with Joshi's ceramic estimate of c. 2300 B.C. Possehl also assigns TF-1295 to IA and TF-1304 & 1309 to IB, the reverse of Joshi 1974 and 1990, following Joshi's 1972 article as Joshi 1974 (pp. 36-37) explains.

syntheses.statement: 'The 14C dating for Surkotada yield an effective time-bracket of c. 2100-1700 B.C.' This is for the whole occupation, not the layout phase alone.
syntheses.disagreement: Uncalibrated, like Joshi's figures; it matches Joshi's 1974 summary of the culture 'between 2100 and 1700 B.C.' (Joshi 1974, p. 34) and is later than Joshi's own c. 2300 B.C. for the foundation.

parts.conflicts: Joshi's own statements of the foundation date differ by method. His radiocarbon range for Sub-period IA is 2055-1970 B.C. (1974, p. 36), or from 2315 B.C. if PRL-85 is accepted (1990, p. 62), while his ceramic cross-dating puts the arrival of Harappans and the founding of Surkotada at c. 2300 B.C. (1974, p. 36; 1990, p. 63); his overall brackets are 2100-1700 B.C. (1974, p. 34), 2300-1750 B.C. (1974, p. 38) and 2300-1700 B.C., which the memoir attributes to 'the absolute chronology offered by C-14 determinations' (1990, pp. 17, 59). The phase of two samples changed between publications: Joshi 1972 put TF-1295 at the top of IA and TF-1304/1309 in IB; Joshi 1974 and 1990 move TF-1295 to the earliest IB and TF-1304/1309 to IA, and reject the latter as a mixed sample. Possehl and Raval 1989 keep the 1972 attributions. Joshi also misprints two ages (TF-1310 as 2810 for 3810; and see the residential annexe part for TF-1295 and PRL-85).

parts.part: residential annexe (lower, eastern enclosure; 'lower city' in the 1970-71 report)
parts.layout_phase: Sub-period IA; rebuilt in stone in Sub-period IC on the same line
parts.what_was_built: In IA, 'Around the residential area was also provided a mud brick fortification having a width of 3.25 m and a gate of which only one arm could be exposed' (Joshi 1990, p. 21). The IA southern rampart is 3.60 to 4 m wide, of 10 x 20 x 40 cm mud bricks; the eastern rampart was 'built over a raised ground of 70 cm with the rubble and mud brick foundation' and stands 2 m high in nineteen courses of mud brick, 4 m wide at the base; an entrance 'of very humble pretentions' with a ramp of rammed earth and mud bricks lay at the south-eastern corner (pp. 44-45). Only the southern side and part of the eastern side were excavated, giving a width of 46 m (p. 44). Inside, the IA levels have a lane 4.20 m wide flanked by houses, with a soakage jar and a covered drain of two phases (p. 45). The 1971-72 report describes the IA residential enclosure as 'located adjacant to the eastern fortification-wall of the citadel' with a 3.25 m mud-brick wall and a gateway (IAR 1971-72, p. 16). In IC the enclosure was rebuilt with a rubble and dressed-stone rampart about 3.40 m wide, a corner bastion and a southern entrance (Joshi 1990, p. 57; IAR 1971-72, p. 17).
parts.excavator_basis: Joshi gives one range for Sub-period IA at the site (see the citadel part): 2055-1970 B.C. from radiocarbon on the 5730-year half-life, uncalibrated, or from 2315 B.C. with PRL-85, with ceramic cross-dating pointing to a foundation by c. 2300 B.C. (Joshi 1974, p. 36; Joshi 1990, pp. 61-63).

radiocarbon.context: Loc ZF1, Qd 2, Layers 13 and 14, depth 4.85m, Field 21
radiocarbon.phase: mid-levels of Period IA (Joshi 1990, p. 62); the date list says only 'Harappa culture'
radiocarbon.note: The list prints '2190 BC' (1950 minus the 5568-year age).

radiocarbon.context: mid-levels of Period I A at a depth of 4.8m B.S from layers 13-14 in Trench ZF1, Qd.2 'which is located in the habitational area of the citadel'
radiocarbon.note: Printed as 'PRL-85, Chalcolithic culture, — (4365±135)—1950 = 2315 B.C.' The page does not state the half-life. The bracketed format is the one Joshi 1974 (p. 36) explains as 5730-year ages, but the equation as printed does not hold: 4365 minus 1950 is 2415, not 2315. 2315 B.C. corresponds to 4265, which is the list's 4140 x 1.03 (4264), so 4365 is probably a misprint for 4265. Because the printed age is inconsistent, we leave the converted fields empty. We place the sample in the residential annexe because Joshi's structural account puts trench ZF1's Period IA house complex (Group 15) in the residential annexe (pp. 36, 45) and the site plan shows Group 15 there; on p. 62 he describes the same trench as the 'habitational area of the citadel', apparently meaning the citadel complex as a whole.

syntheses.statement: As for the citadel: the calibrated IA dates are taken to show that 'the Urban Phase Sindhi Harappans settled in Gujarat, including Kutch, ca. 2500-2300 B.C.'
syntheses.disagreement: As for the citadel: earlier than Joshi's uncalibrated 2055-1970 B.C., and TF-1295 is placed in IA rather than IB.

parts.conflicts: Excavator and season reports agree that the residential annexe was walled from the beginning, in Sub-period IA, and that its enclosure kept the same area to the end (Joshi 1990, p. 17; IAR 1970-71, p. 13; IAR 1971-72, p. 16). The dating conflicts are those given for the citadel part, together with the misprints in Joshi's figures for PRL-85 and TF-1295 described in the notes to those entries.

first_occupation.basis: The first occupants were already Harappans who built the citadel and the walled residential annexe: 'the earliest occupants of Surkotada were Harappans having some affiliation with antecedent culture' (Joshi 1990, p. 21; IAR 1971-72, p. 13). First occupation and layout phase are therefore the same. The range is Joshi's radiocarbon range for IA on the 5730-year half-life, uncalibrated (Joshi 1974, p. 36), which Joshi 1990 (p. 62) extends to 2315 B.C. with PRL-85; by ceramic cross-dating he dates the foundation to c. 2300 B.C. (1974, p. 36; 1990, p. 63). Possehl and Raval's calibration puts the arrival of Harappans in Kutch at c. 2500-2300 B.C. (1989, p. 10).
first_occupation.locator: joshi1974puratattva pp. 34-36; joshi1990surkotada pp. 17, 21, 59-63; iar1971-72 p. 13

notes: Surkotada is a small fortified Harappan settlement of two adjoining walled enclosures, a higher citadel on the west and a lower residential annexe on the east, excavated by J. P. Joshi in 1970-71 and 1971-72. The 1970-71 report called the sequence Periods I, II and III; after the second season it was relabelled Sub-periods IA, IB and IC (IAR 1971-72, p. 13; Joshi 1990, p. 15). Both enclosures were walled in mud brick and mud lumps on rammed-earth platforms in IA, the first occupation, and kept their area through IB. In IC they were rebuilt in rubble and dressed stone with corner bastions and the southern gateway complex of the citadel, so the masonry visible today is IC work on IA lines (Joshi 1990, pp. 17, 21, 49-50, 57). The radiocarbon dates come from the Tata Institute and the Physical Research Laboratory. The Radiocarbon date lists print conventional ages on the 5568-year half-life and 'B.C.' values that are simply 1950 minus those ages. Joshi prints, for the same samples, the 5568 age followed by the 5730-year age in brackets and a B.C. date equal to the 5730 age minus 1950, and he states the 5730 convention in 1974 (p. 36). None of these B.C. figures is calibrated. Possehl and Raval (1989) give calibrated ranges, without stating the curve or confidence level for each range. Joshi's reprints contain several misprints (TF-1310, TF-1295, PRL-85), described in the individual entries; where Joshi 1990 reprints the 1974 figures unchanged we record only the 1974 printing, which states its half-life. We include every IA determination, TF-1295 (whose phase, end of IA or start of IB, is disputed), and TF-1301 (assigned only to 'Period I'). The four Sub-period IC dates (TF-1297, TF-1311, TF-1294, TF-1307; Joshi 1974, p. 38) date the stone rebuilding of the walls, not their first construction, and are omitted. The IA deposits begin on a raised rammed-earth platform over natural soil (Joshi 1990, pp. 36-38), so no earlier phase exists to date. Not consulted: Joshi 1972 in the Journal of the Oriental Institute, Baroda 22 (not found online), and Possehl's compilations of 1999 and 2002. Ramachandran 1975 and Mandal 1972, two radiocarbon compilations, contain no Surkotada entry. No Bayesian model has been published. The site plans in Joshi 1990 show a north arrow; per our brief we did not record orientation.
